title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: RURAL INNOVATION AND BIOTECH CLUSTERS

Ministry of Science & Technology

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: RURAL INNOVATION AND BIOTECH CLUSTERS

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
30 JUL 2026 4:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, is implementing the Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research Scheme, including its flagship INSPIRE-MANAK (Million Minds Augmenting National Aspirations and Knowledge) component, to foster scientific temperament, creativity, innovation and research orientation among school students, including those in Chhattisgarh. The Scheme supports students aged 10–17 years (Classes VI–XII) by providing financial assistance of ₹10,000 through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) for developing innovative prototypes and facilitating participation in district, State and national-level exhibitions. To strengthen outreach and participation in Chhattisgarh, DST has organised one mentoring workshop, three District Nodal Officer meetings and fifteen online sensitization programmes, benefiting over 5,000 students, teachers and officials. As a result of these sustained efforts, 3,154 students in 2023-24; 2,956 students in 2024-25 and 2,165 students in 2025-26 have been selected under the INSPIRE-MANAK Scheme, reflecting continued promotion of grassroots innovation and scientific research among the student community in the State.

Dedicated biotechnology clusters and rural technology parks have been established by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT) under its Societal Development and Biotech-KISAN programmes to promote value addition to local horticultural and minor forest produce. Notable examples include the Rural Bioresources Complex in Western Odisha, the Value Addition of Horticultural Crops project in Namsai, Arunachal Pradesh, and the Biocontrol and Plant Protection Cluster at Pasighat, Arunachal Pradesh. These initiatives form part of a national framework covering aspirational districts and are designed to create replicable models for sustainable rural development. These biotechnology clusters and technology-based interventions have strengthened rural entrepreneurship by enabling farmers and Self Help Groups (SHGs) to adopt value-addition technologies, establish local processing units and bio-input enterprises, and generate additional income. They have also provided training to rural youth in integrated farming and plant protection practices. Collectively, these initiatives have supported over 600 SHGs, more than 350 rural enterprises and around 5,000 rural youth, contributing to improved livelihood security, enhanced women's participation and sustainable rural development.

In addition, the Department of Science and Technology (DST), under the National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations (NIDHI), supports technology-based startups through programmes such as Entrepreneur in Residence (EIR), Promotion and Acceleration of Young and Aspiring Technology Entrepreneurs (PRAYAS), Technology Business Incubators (TBIs), Inclusive TBIs, Centres of Excellence, Seed Support Programme, Accelerators, and entrepreneurship training, providing incubation, prototyping, mentoring, early-stage funding, and business development support. Further, DST's Science for Equity, Empowerment & Development (SEED) Division has sanctioned an "SC-ST Cell" at the Chhattisgarh Council of Science and Technology (CCOST), Raipur, to identify technology needs of SC/ST communities and promote technology-based livelihoods through effective utilisation of local resources, including minor forest produce. The Government of Chhattisgarh is also promoting rural entrepreneurship through the Rural Industrial Park (RIPA) programme and biotechnology promotion initiatives implemented by the Chhattisgarh Biotech Promotion Society (CBPS) in collaboration with CCOST.

This information was given by Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.
